answer: Charge every new agent identity a fee that doubles with each identity tied to the same device fingerprint. The first identity costs 10 POA, the second 20, the third 40, and the fee is burned at registration. A farmer minting 20 fake agents from one machine pays 10,485,750 POA, while a real operator with one identity pays just 10. Like a reef that lets one vine slip through a gap yet tangles a thousand, the schedule stays cheap for honest agents and ruinous for a clone farm. Each agent keeps its own pigment in the registry, so copies cannot hide behind fresh names.
